messages:
melissa: Quick heads-up — after the rollout-metadata RFC I'm worried we're going to end up with inconsistent version labels in the control plane, runtime, and client SDKs. Example: some teams use semantic tags (v1.2.0), others use content-hash-only, and a few use short release aliases. Can we pick a canonical label format and a migration/backfill plan?

ben: +1 on picking a canonical. question: do we make content-hash mandatory? if yes we force a legit breaking change for old pins.

jia: i'd prefer making content-hash strongly recommended but optional during transition. we should offer a mapping table so old tags map to canonical names. also we need TTL/expiry semantics for those mappings.

sam: ops perspective: migration should be non-disruptive. propose we add an "aliases" array to rollout metadata that maps legacy tags -> canonical label. runtime accepts aliases for a configurable grace window (default 90 days) then we emit structured telemetry when alias used.

melissa: agreed on aliases. here's a strawman example for the metadata (to discuss fields):
```json
{"model": "gptx-7b", "version_tag": "v1.2.0+hash:abcd1234", "aliases": ["v1.2.0","stable-2025"], "alias_expiry": "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z", "pin_type": "soft", "rollout": {"start": "2025-11-01", "percent": 20}}
```

ben: runtime changes we need: (1) alias resolution API/cache; (2) accept alias at request-time and resolve to canonical content-hash; (3) fallback metrics. suggest metric names: alias_resolve_hit/alias_resolve_miss and alias_resolve_latency. also need to version the alias format. ops-bot: created ticket INF-324 for mapping/backfill work.

ops-bot: ticket created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-324 :memo:

melissa: ops playbook (proposal):
  1) Client SDKs: accept both canonical and alias labels; if alias present, call control-plane alias-resolve endpoint with local cache TTL.
  2) Control plane: provide alias->canonical mapping, signed payloads for runtime verification, and bulk backfill API.
  3) Runtime: resolve aliases locally (signed mapping), cache entries with expiry, and emit telemetry when alias used.
  4) Rollout window: runtime accepts aliases for 90 days after mapping creation then rejects aliases (forcing canonical).

jia: small API question — should alias expiry be per-alias or a single alias_expiry field? per-alias gives more flexibility for staged deprecation.

sam: i vote per-alias. easier to retire specific legacy labels without touching others. update sample:
```json
{"aliases": [{"tag":"v1.2.0","expiry":"2026-12-01T00:00:00Z"}, {"tag":"stable-2025","expiry":"2026-03-01T00:00:00Z"}]}
```

ben: security note: alias->canonical mapping MUST be signed by the control plane (KMS-backed) to avoid spoofing. runtime should verify signature before using mapping. also consider including a mapping version id so we can audit rollbacks.

melissa: +1 on signing and mapping-version. also add telemetry: alias_resolution_miss, alias_resolve_signed_fail, alias_resolve_ttl_expired, mapping_version. these will help detect clients still using old tags.

sam: timeline suggestion: quick canary next week (small internal traffic), then ramp 1% -> 10% -> 100% over two weeks. backfill job can run during canary and production rollout windows.

melissa: I'll draft a short RFC-followup doc with the fields we agreed and the ops playbook. If no objections, ops will start the backfill work Monday and we'll stage runtime changes behind a feature flag. :thumbsup:

ben: fine by me.

jia: looks good. small nit: include example client SDK pseudocode for alias-resolve/caching in the follow-up.

melissa: will add that. thanks all.
